Prose:
Scarface’s silence broke into a sharp command. He gestured toward the cell door with a jerky motion of his scarred hand, dismissing the girl’s clinging fingers as irrelevant data points in his ledger of assets.

The guard obeyed instantly. The iron keyring jangled sharply as it disengaged the primary shackles on Caelen’s wrists. The metal links fell away, leaving only loose cuffs that rattled against his forearms—a deliberate delay that felt like a cruel joke, granting the girl one final moment of contact before they were dragged forward.

For a heartbeat, the girl’s small hands dug into Caelen’s skin again, her nails pressing white-knuckled into the rough leather of his tunic as she refused to let go. He tried to pull himself up on the loose shackles, but his broad palms scraped uselessly against the damp stone floor. Every movement felt heavier than before; gravity was a stubborn anchor dragging at his limbs, making him feel like he were wading through molasses. But the guard’s strength was overwhelming, hauling him toward the exit with mechanical efficiency.

They were dragged toward the door, the girl’s weeping now audible to the guards but ignored as mere background noise. She sobbed openly, her voice tearing through the oppressive silence of the cell, yet no one looked back. Caelen felt the cold indifference of the purple-robed overseer, who sat absorbed in his ledger near the cell entrance, treating their separation as a bureaucratic formality rather than a tragedy.

As they moved, the physical distance between them stretched, severing the fragile connection she represented—the only proof that someone here cared enough to cry over another. The realization settled heavily on him: shielding her had not saved her; it had made them both visible targets, transparent and vulnerable in the eyes of men who ruled by arbitrary will.

The guard ignored her pleas, his boots crunching softly on gravel outside the stone walls, while Scarface watched them go with an expressionless mask, waiting to see what value they held for the auction.
